title: Labcorp Collaborates with OHSU on Clinical Study Evaluating MRD Testing in Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer
body_markdown:
*Investigator-led research will evaluate whether blood-based monitoring can provide earlier insight into disease recurrence following treatment*


**BURLINGTON, N.C. Sept. 9, 2026** —[Labcorp](http://www.labcorp.com/) (NYSE: LH), a global leader of innovative and comprehensive laboratory services, today announced a collaboration with the Knight Cancer Institute at Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU), Oregon's only academic health center, on an investigator-led[clinical study](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07726602?locStr=Oregon&country=US&state=Oregon&cond=Bladder%20Cancer&viewType=Card&term=TiMBER&rank=1) evaluating the use of molecular residual disease (MRD) testing to help identify disease recurrence earlier in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) following treatment.


Muscle-invasive bladder cancer is an aggressive form of bladder cancer with a[significant risk](https://www.clinical-genitourinary-cancer.com/article/S1558-7673(25)00166-1/fulltext) of recurrence after treatment intended to cure the disease. While patients are routinely monitored following treatment, current surveillance methods may not always detect signs of recurrence at the earliest stages. The study will evaluate whether[Labcorp Plasma Detect® Genome MRD Ultra](https://www.labcorp.com/oncology/providers/testing-solutions/solid-tumor/mrd) , a new, next-generation, whole-genome sequencing-based test, can help identify recurrence earlier by detecting low levels of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in blood.


"Advancing precision oncology requires strong collaboration between academic cancer centers and diagnostics innovators," said Jen-Jane Liu, M.D., Chief of Urologic Oncology at OHSU and Knight Cancer Center and principal investigator of the study. "By working with Labcorp on this study, we have the opportunity to evaluate the potential of tumor-informed MRD testing in a patient population where recurrence remains a significant clinical challenge despite advances in treatment."


The collaboration brings together Labcorp's scientific expertise in developing innovative diagnostic solutions and OHSU and the Knight Cancer Center's leadership in cancer care as a National Cancer Institute-designated cancer center. Together, the organizations aim to advance understanding of how MRD testing may support more personalized treatment strategies and generate evidence needed to guide future clinical practice.


"MRD has the potential to fundamentally change how we monitor patients after cancer treatment by giving clinicians a more sensitive view of residual disease and recurrence risk," said Shakti Ramkissoon, M.D., Ph.D., senior vice president, enterprise oncology at Labcorp. "Our collaboration with OHSU expands Labcorp's ongoing efforts to better understand how tumor-informed MRD testing can be used to monitor cancer recurrence and inform personalized treatment plans. Together with leading academic medical centers and cancer research institutions, we are building the evidence base for MRD testing across a range of tumor types."


**Advancing Evidence for MRD Testing**
The study builds on Labcorp's growing body of MRD research and collaborations focused on evaluating the role of tumor-informed ctDNA testing across cancer care. Recent milestones include[research](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/press-releases/labcorpr-plasma-detecttm-clinical-studies-featured-nature) published in *Nature Medicine* and *Clinical Cancer Research* demonstrating the ability of Plasma Detect to inform treatment strategies and advance cancer research, as well as the[expansion](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/press-releases/labcorp-expands-mrd-testing-breast-lung-and-colon-cancer) of Plasma Detect testing to breast, lung and colon cancers. Together, these efforts are helping establish the evidence base for MRD testing across tumor types and clinical settings.


To learn more about the study, visit[https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07726602?locStr=Oregon&country=US&state=Oregon&cond=Bladder%20Cancer&viewType=Card&term=TiMBER&rank=1](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07726602?locStr=Oregon&country=US&state=Oregon&cond=Bladder%20Cancer&viewType=Card&term=TiMBER&rank=1) .


For more information on Labcorp's MRD portfolio, visit[https://www.labcorp.com/oncology/providers/testing-solutions/solid-tumor/mrd](https://www.labcorp.com/oncology/providers/testing-solutions/solid-tumor/mrd) .
